resources.string: Turn this screen into a second display. Connect from your Mac and we’ll take it from here.
Preparing this screen for your Mac. Just a moment.
Making the connection. Your desktop will appear automatically.
Start Extend or Mirror in OpenDisplay on your Mac. Your desktop will appear here automatically.
Connect this device and your Mac to the same Wi-Fi or local network. You can also use a USB cable.
We couldn’t reach your Mac. Check that OpenDisplay is open and both devices are on the same network.
This device couldn’t start listening. Close and reopen OpenDisplay to try again.
Update OpenDisplay on your Mac and this device, then connect again.
Connect your Mac and this device to the same Wi-Fi or LAN.
Choose this device, then start Extend or Mirror.
Enable USB debugging on this device and allow your Mac when prompted.
Choose Android USB, then start Extend or Mirror.
Settings couldn’t be opened. Open your device settings to continue.
In OpenDisplay on your Mac, choose Connect over network and enter an address below.
No network address yet. Join Wi-Fi or a local network, then check here again.
Pick what you need. We’ll keep it simple.
My Mac can’t find this device

Keep OpenDisplay open on both devices and use the same network. Guest Wi-Fi can block connections between devices.\n\nIf this device isn’t listed on your Mac, choose Connect over network and enter this device’s address.
Wi-Fi won’t connect with a VPN

In device Settings → Network & internet → VPN, tap the gear beside your VPN. Check “Block connections without VPN”: it can block your Mac even when the VPN looks disconnected. Turning it off allows connections outside the VPN.\n\nAlso allow local network access in your VPN app. If you prefer to keep VPN lockdown enabled, try USB debugging instead.

1. In device Settings → About, tap Build number seven times to enable Developer options.

2. In Settings → System → Developer options, enable USB debugging.

3. Connect a data cable to your Mac. Unlock this device and accept the debugging prompt.

4. In OpenDisplay on your Mac, choose Android USB. The Mac needs Android platform-tools (adb) installed.

USB debugging keeps your Mac’s Wi-Fi connection available.

After connecting a data cable, open USB preferences and choose Connected device under USB controlled by. Enable USB tethering in Network & internet → Hotspot & tethering.\n\nChoose Android USB in OpenDisplay on your Mac. USB tethering can change your Mac’s internet route; if needed, put Wi-Fi first in macOS Network Service Order.
Use touch on your Mac display

Tap to click. Drag to move. Use two fingers to scroll.

Pinch to zoom, then pan around. Double-tap to reset the zoom.

Sound plays through this device when enabled on your Mac.
Choose Extend or Mirror on your Mac. The screen switches to your desktop as soon as it arrives.
First time? Allow Screen Recording on your Mac. Allow Accessibility to use touch input.
